title: Classification
blurb: Recognising the dominant operation before acting.

groups.title: The Five Basic Forms
groups.blurb: Recognition in unambiguous cases. Foundation before the misleading forms.

skills.name: Sum
skills.note: Dominant op = the outermost $+$; its terms are the chunks.

skills.name: Difference
skills.note: The last operation applied is subtraction. The chunks are the two terms.

skills.name: Product
skills.note: Dominant op = the outermost $\cdot$; its factors are the chunks.

skills.name: Quotient
skills.note: The last operation applied is division. The chunks are numerator and denominator.

skills.name: Power
skills.note: Dominant op = the power; base and exponent are the chunks.

groups.title: Misleading Surface Forms
groups.blurb: Where a visible operation distracts from the dominant one. The core of Skill 2.

skills.name: Sum of products — multiplication is inside the terms
skills.note: The multiplications are inside the terms, already done. The last operation applied to the whole expression is addition — a sum.

skills.name: Product containing a sum — looks like a sum
skills.note: The $+$ is trapped inside a chunk (the bracket). The dominant operation is the multiplication outside — a product.

skills.name: Coefficient in front of a power
skills.note: $2x^2$ is $2 \cdot (x^2)$, not $(2x)^2$. The exponent grabs only the $x$; the dominant operation is the product of $2$ and $x^2$.

skills.name: Expression with a leading minus
skills.note: A leading minus is just the sign of the first term — it does not make the whole thing a subtraction. -3x + 2y is a sum. (A leading minus can also sit on a power, e.g. -(x+1)², which is a power then negated.)

skills.name: Power containing a sum
skills.note: The base is the whole chunk (x+1). The dominant operation is the power.

skills.name: Quotient with a complex numerator or denominator
skills.note: The sums are inside the chunks (numerator and denominator). The whole thing is a division — a quotient.

skills.name: Difference of two squares
skills.note: Dominant operation: a difference. The shape is special — both chunks are perfect squares ($9 = 3^2$, $4x^2 = (2x)^2$). Recognising it unlocks factoring as $(a+b)(a-b)$.

skills.name: Perfect square trinomial
skills.note: Dominant operation: a sum of three terms. The shape is special: the middle term is twice the product of the roots of the outer terms. Recognising it unlocks writing as (a±b)².

skills.name: Common factor
skills.note: Dominant operation: a sum. The shape is special: all chunks share a factor (3, a, 2x, (x+1)). Recognising it unlocks factoring it out.

skills.name: Linear form
skills.note: Dominant operation: a sum. Highest power is 1 — one variable term and one constant. The linear shape.

skills.name: Quadratic form
skills.note: Dominant operation: a sum. Highest power is 2 — the quadratic shape. Recognising it gates all of quadratic algebra.
